raw.product_description: Narma is an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" designed for AI-first companies. It functions through a three-layered architecture: an Intelligence Layer (Layer 2) that detects employee intent, business value of tasks, and workflow "drift," and an Execution Layer (Layer 3) which is an "Agent Factory" that generates, deploys, and monitors AI agents for high-ROI opportunities. The system leverages existing foundation models and focuses on understanding the "Work Graph" to identify areas where AI can assist.
raw.core_excitement: The founder is excited about creating a single system that can intelligently observe work, decide AI actions, and continuously auto-build agents to ensure "Continuous AI lift" for AI-first companies.

raw.thesis: Narma is creating an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" for AI-first companies. This brain aims to observe how work is done, identify opportunities for AI intervention, and continuously deploy AI agents to automate high-ROI tasks within existing workflows. The innovation lies in its three-layered architecture that focuses on detecting employee intent and "drift" in work processes, rather than building new foundation models. The target user is AI-first companies that struggle to implement and measure the impact of AI automation at scale due to a lack of telemetry, unreliable ROI measurement, and constant workflow drift. This venture matters because these issues prevent AI-first companies from realizing the full potential of AI automation, leading to wasted resources and missed opportunities for efficiency gains. The founder's goal appears to be a growth startup, given the focus on "deploy AI automation at scale" and addressing enterprise-level problems. The venture is currently at the idea stage, with a detailed description of the concept and architecture but no mention of development or user traction. The venture is positioned to complement existing foundation models by building an intelligence and execution layer on top of them, rather than replacing them. It aims to integrate with and enhance current enterprise AI strategies by providing a missing "brain" for orchestration and continuous improvement.
